title: Cars, Trains or Planes How Do Europeans Travel
paragraphs: How do people in Europe get from one place to another? New numbers show that the car is still by far the most popular choice, but trains and planes are becoming more important.

In September 2026, Eurostat, the European Union's statistics office, published information about travel in the EU in 2024. It measured the total distance that people traveled by each type of transportation.
According to Eurostat, cars made up 69.2% of all passenger travel in the EU in 2024. However, this number is slowly getting smaller. It fell by 2.9 percentage points between 2014 and 2024.

Trains made up 7.5% of travel, and buses and coaches made up 7.3%. This was the first time since 2014 that more people traveled by train than by bus. Train travel grew by 0.9 points in 10 years, but bus travel fell by 1.3 points. Air travel grew the fastest of all, rising by 3.6 points. Travel by ship was only 0.4%.

There were big differences between countries. In Lithuania, cars made up 83.7% of travel, the highest number in the EU. Cars were also very popular in the Netherlands and Finland. In Croatia, on the other hand, almost half of all travel, 45.6%, was by plane. This is probably because Croatia has many islands and many tourists. Planes were also popular in Bulgaria and Cyprus.

Trains were most popular in Hungary, at 11.3%, and Austria, at just over 10%. Buses were popular in Malta, Ireland and Hungary, where there are fewer train lines. Travel by ship was most common in Estonia, Malta and Croatia, but it was still small in all three countries.
